requirement:
For each changed record, `habeas refactor` MUST rewrite every recorded file,
selector, definition name, definition selection, and match the mappings cover,
including the `citations`, `requirement`, `file`, and `item` fields of citation
and site reviews, and MUST record the current text, hash, and reference-set
digest where it rewrote the corresponding field.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.refactor.record_fields` has no structural obligation, so no implementation root is needed. It has test edges and no implementation edges or review roots.

I checked each clause for a structural reading:
- "MUST rewrite every recorded file, selector, definition name, definition selection, and match the mappings cover, including the `citations`, `requirement`, `file`, and `item` fields of citation and site reviews". This says which record fields end up rewritten. Any code that produces the same rewritten records meets it. That includes one pass or several, a generic field walker or per-field code, and any helper layout. A different factoring has the same observable behavior and still satisfies the text.
- "MUST record the current text, hash, and reference-set digest where it rewrote the corresponding field". This describes the values stored in the output records. It names no hashing algorithm, library, type, signature, or interface to delegate to. A different way of computing or storing them gives the same results and still satisfies the text.

The requirement names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field layout, or named interface that the implementation must use. Every clause describes observable behavior, which the tests on this requirement cover. The behavioral criterion judges test adequacy, so I did not assess it here.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.refactor.record_fields`. Each test asserts the rewritten fields. Most also run the project's validation (`errors(root)`, `citation_errors`, `site_errors`) after the refactor. A rewritten text, hash or digest that was wrong would fail that validation.

- **Recorded file and selector.**
  - `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_function_keeps_its_evidence_current]` moves `fn[load]` to another file. It asserts `inputs[1].file` and the rewritten rationale, and validation passes afterwards.
  - `tests/refactor.rs#fn[versioned_records_preserve_sdk_dependencies_across_verified_moves]` covers the "file" scenario (a whole-file rename) and the "selector" scenario (`fn[load]` to `mod[loading]/fn[load]`). It also covers requirement rename, "move" and "extra" scenarios, and each ends with clean validation.
- **Definition name.** `a_moved_term_rewrites_definition_inputs_and_the_texts_using_it` asserts `inputs[1].definition == "glossary.term"`. `a_citation_reviews_commentary_follows_a_renamed_requirement` asserts `inputs[2].definition == "glossary.word"`.
- **Definition selection and matches.** `a_moved_chapter_rewrites_glob_selections_and_their_matches` maps the chapter `rules=core`. It asserts the `requirements` glob becomes `core.*` and `matches` becomes `["core.check","core.load"]`. Validation is clean afterwards.
- **Citation review fields.**
  - `a_citation_review_follows_its_item_and_the_name_it_cites` moves the item to another file and module and renames the cited requirement. It compares the moved record, including `file`, `item` and `citations`, with an independently built expected record.
  - `a_citation_reviews_commentary_follows_a_renamed_requirement` asserts `record["citations"]` equals the expected value with the commentary's term renamed.
- **Site review fields.** `src/refactor/tests.rs#fn[site_reviews_follow_their_site_and_renamed_requirement]` asserts `requirement == "rules.rule"`, `file == "src/other.rs"` and `item == "mod[checks]/fn[check_two]"` on the moved record. It also asserts the old directory is gone and site validation errors are empty.
- **Current text, hash and reference-set digest where a field was rewritten.**
  - The `requirement` text is asserted in `a_moved_term_rewrites_definition_inputs_and_the_texts_using_it`.
  - The citation test compares the moved inputs, including the requirement-input text, with expected values.
  - In the versioned-records test, expected dependencies are built independently. Every input hash is a SHA-256 of the input, and the reference-set digest comes from `record["references"]`. The test asserts `migrated == expected`, including the per-criterion dependencies.
  - Validation passing after each move checks that the stored hashes and digests are current.

The tests include the negative cases "edit" and "bad-extra", where the record is left unchanged. These belong to `requirements.refactor.edited_while_moving` and `requirements.refactor.whole_record`, not to this requirement.

I found no obligation without a test and no marking gap. Every test above carries a `{test}` reference to the subject.

text: For each changed record, `habeas refactor` MUST rewrite every recorded file,
selector, definition name, definition selection, and match the mappings cover,
including the `citations`, `requirement`, `file`, and `item` fields of citation
and site reviews, and MUST record the current text, hash, and reference-set
digest where it rewrote the corresponding field.
A requirements or definition input MUST be rewritten only if the
{term}`requirements.refactor.mapped_back` current text of each definition it
records equals the recorded text and, for a requirements input, the mapped
selection's current matches are exactly the recorded matches with the mapping
The *mapped-back* form of current text or a current address is the text or
address with each new side of the mappings replaced by its old side.
